ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, it is known that $AB=6$, $BC=8$. The perpendicular bisector of $BD$ intersects $AD$ at point $E$ and intersects $BC$ at point $F$. What is the length of $BF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}
Given that quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle,\\
$\therefore \angle A=90^\circ$, AB=6, AD=BC=8,\\
$\therefore$BD=$\sqrt{AB^{2}+AD^{2}}=10$,\\
Additionally, since EF is the perpendicular bisector of BD,\\
$\therefore$OB=OD=5, $\angle$BOF=$90^\circ$,\\
Also, $\because \angle C=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \triangle BOF\sim \triangle BCD$,\\
$\therefore \frac{BO}{BC}=\frac{BF}{BD}$, that is: $\frac{5}{8}=\frac{BF}{10}$, solving this yields: $BF=\boxed{\frac{25}{4}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is rectangle ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right; BD is the diagonal from the lower-left B to the upper-right D. Another straight line EF goes from E on the upper side AD through the interior point O to F on the lower side BC, and is perpendicular to BD at O, indicating that EF is the perpendicular bisector of BD. Then reason: Establish a coordinate system according to the position of the figure, let B=(0,0), C=(8,0), A=(0,6), D=(8,6). The midpoint of line segment BD is O=((0+8)/2,(0+6)/2)=(4,3). The slope of BD is (6-0)/(8-0)=3/4, so the slope of its perpendicular bisector EF is -4/3. EF passes through O, therefore the equation is y-3=-(4/3)(x-4). Point F is on BC, so y=0. Substituting gives 0-3=-(4/3)(x-4), that is, 3=(4/3)(x-4), so x-4=9/4, x=25/4. Because B is at the origin and F is on the x-axis, BF is equal to the abscissa distance of F, namely 25/4.
